About the Opportunity 
 
 About the Institute 
 Do you want to be part of an exciting new Institute focused on combining human and machine intelligence into working AI solutions? 
  
We are building a pioneering research and innovation hub in AI—one that will shape the way humans and machines collaborate for decades to come. Led by Prof. Samuel V. Scarpino, the Institute for Experiential AI is built around the challenges and opportunities made possible by human-machine collaboration. The Institute provides a framework to design, implement, and scale AI-driven technologies in ways that make a true difference to society. Our ability to respond to the opportunities afforded to society will depend on training and building a workforce that is AI-capable and prosperous. 
  
Founded in 1898, Northeastern is a global research university and the recognized leader in experience-driven lifelong learning. Our world-renowned experiential approach empowers our students, faculty, alumni, and partners to create impact far beyond the confines of discipline, degree, and campus. 

 The Culture 
 Here at the Institute for Experiential AI (EAI) we are committed to the highest standards in all we do. Working at the EAI offers opportunities, an environment, and a culture that just isn’t found together anywhere else. This is the right place for you if you’re curious, motivated by the future of technology, and want to be part of a unique and diverse community that works on high-impact research, educational, business, and societal problems. 

 Job Summary: 
 This is a 1-year fixed term appointment, renewable based on available funding. 

 Northeastern University's Institute for Experiential AI is recruiting for a ML Engineer with special focus on physical AI systems, knowledge aggregation and Ai for control and optimization for a DOE Genesis project led by Dr. Ayan Paul. The ML Engineer will be based at the Boston campus, MA, conduct applied research, prepare work for submission to journal/conference publications, and contribute to extramural funding applications. This position has a three-year appointment, renewable yearly subject to availability of funding. The ML Engineer will work on projects that will include developing AI models, large-scale agentic systems, knowledge aggregation systems, and fine-tuning language models. Participation in this project will include scientific programming, data analysis, training AI models, manuscript preparation, meeting with collaborators, mentoring graduate students, etc.  

 About the project: CLARA (Cognitive Layered Agentic Reasoning for ARIS) is a three-year, Genesis Mission Phase II project led by Northeastern University with MSU/FRIB and Gravitate AI. It will build an agentic AI system for operating the Advanced Rare Isotope Separator (ARIS) at FRIB. 

 ARIS operations are limited by the gap between LISE++ simulations and observed beam behavior. As a result, weekly beam development takes 16 to 24 hours, about half of which goes to manual isotope calibration. Planning a new experiment takes about 20 days, and no predictive monitoring exists for roughly 200 time-correlated machine parameters. 

 CLARA addresses this with three objectives: 
 Planning and tuning. Bayesian optimization uses LISE++ as a physics-informed prior, alongside paired forward and inverse neural surrogates trained on simulation and EPICS archive data. These power a Planning Agent for non-experts and an Expert Tuning Agent. 
 Calibration. Diffeomorphic image registration maps simulated particle identification (PID) distributions to measured ones from a single measurement. 
 Monitoring and knowledge. Quickest Change Detection models (classical CuSum and a transformer-based DeepQCD) and a hazardous-configuration classifier make up a Safety Agent with gated beam-interrupt authority. A Critic module commits validated tunes to a knowledge graph built with eGoT. 
 
 The targets are reducing experiment planning time to 1 to 2 days, beam development time to about 4 hours, and thus facilitating 500 to 800 extra beam hours per year. The project aims to advance from TRL 3 to TRL 6–7 and to validate transfer to at least one non-ARIS separator. 

 The ML Engineer hired for this position will work with Benjamin Gyori at Khoury College, Deniz Erdogmus at the College of Engineering, and Ayan Paul at EAI and is expected to develop AI algorithms, RAG pipelines and agentic systems for the Genesis project, collaborate with the FRIB experiment at the Michigan State University and Gravitate AI. 

 Minimum Qualifications: 
 An MS or PhD in computer science, computer engineering, physics and allied fields with a heavy focus on machine learning, agentic systems, RAG construction and development by the appointment start date. 
 At least 1 year of research or work experience in an academic group. Corporate experience will be considered if it is aligned with the job role. 
 A record of outstanding research, as evidenced by software outputs, and other scholarly measures of impact. 
 Strong, demonstrable background in machine learning and AI. Must have demonstrable experience in AI model development, LLM and knowledge graphs. 
 Should have 1+ years of experience in developing agentic systems, graph databases and/or developing data preprocessing pipelines and AI model training on high-performance computing. 
 Must have familiarity with knowledge graphs, agentic systems and metrics for assessing performance of RAG systems. 
 Preferably have experience in developing deep neural networks for computer vision, tabular data anocessing. 
 Must have experience in research software development, FAIR data/open science. 
 
 Values & Abilities: 
 We expect ML Engineers to establish and advocate for best practices in scientific reproducibility of all results, and to promote the ethical use of data and algorithms. 
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 
 Respect for diversity and the importance of interdisciplinary teams. 
 Entrepreneurial mindset, self-starter, and innovative thinker while at the same time being able to navigate multi-layered channels within a university setting and work across multiple projects. 
 Team-player who can collaborate effectively in a university setting and with corporate partners. 
 Open-minded, assertive, and professional when collaborating and working within our team and with other groups within Northeastern University. 
 
 Key Responsibilities & Accountabilities: 
 (90%) Co-develop, collaboratively lead and participate in research projects that advance scientific knowledge and solve relevant societal and industrial problems. Participation in these projects will include working with graduate or undergraduate students, scientific programming, data analysis, manuscript preparation, meeting with collaborators, etc. 
 (5%) Represent the university in conferences, seminars, and other public events. 
 (5%) Other assignments as deemed necessary 
 
 Required Documents : 
 Please submit the following documents in a single Word/PDF document along with your application: 
 Cover Letter 
 Resume (Please include contact information of referees for at least three letters of reference) 
 A one page statement on how your interest and experience align with the requirements of the work. 
 
 Position Type 
 
Research 
 Additional Information 
 
 Northeastern University considers factors such as candidate work experience, education and skills when extending an offer.  
 
 Northeastern has a comprehensive benefits package for benefit eligible employees. This includes medical, vision, dental, paid time off, tuition assistance, wellness & life, retirement- as well as commuting & transportation. Visit https://hr.northeastern.edu/benefits/ for more information.    
 




 All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply and will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, disability status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
 
 
 
 Compensation Grade/Pay Type: 
110S 
 Expected Hiring Range: 
$76,335.00 - $107,823.75 
 With the pay range(s) shown above, the starting salary will depend on several factors, which may include your education, experience, location, knowledge and expertise, and skills as well as a pay comparison to similarly-situated employees already in the role. Salary ranges are reviewed regularly and are subject to change.
